```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(latex2exp)
library(cowplot)
library(gridExtra)
```

Take care of the legend

```{r}
# Exemple simulé si tu n’as pas défini `simul_data`
set.seed(123)
simul_data <- data.frame(
  x = rnorm(100),
  y = rnorm(100),
  `Confidence.Bands` = rep(c("90%", "68%"), each = 50)
  # ,
  # `Identification` = rep(c("Cholesky", "IV"), 50)
)

# Définir le mapping manuel pour les types de traits
#linetype <- c("Cholesky" = "dashed", "IV" = "solid")

# Plot avec légende uniquement
plot_legend <- ggplot(data = simul_data, aes(x = x)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(fill = `Confidence.Bands`), bins = 30, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = y)) +#, linetype = `Identification`)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("90%" = "blue", "68%" = "lightblue"),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  # scale_linetype_manual(
  #   values = linetype,
  #   name = "Identification",
  #   drop = FALSE
  # ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.box = "horizontal"
  )

# Extraire la légende personnalisée
custom_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(plot_legend)
#custom_legend <- get_plot_component(plot_legend, "guide-box", return_all = TRUE)[[3]]

#custom_legend[[3]]
#custom_legend
```


```{r}
#solution <-gen_benchmark

plot_irf_from_gen_benchmark <- function(solution, #irf_cholesky,
                                        variable_names = NULL, shock="price" ) {
  if (shock == "price"){
   shock_label = "$P_{elec}$ shock IRF"
  }else if (shock == "gen"){
    shock_label = "$Q_{elec}$ shock IRF"
  }else{
    return("Invalid shock type. Please use 'price' or 'quantity'.")
  }
  index <- grep(shock, solution$headers_var)
  lambda_name <- sprintf("lambda_0%d", index)
  
  lambda_0 <- solution$lambda_0
  #lambda_0 <- solution$median_50
  #lambda_0_chol <-irf_cholesky$irf
  # lambda_0_chol <- irf_cholesky
  
  # lambda_0_chol <- array(unlist(lambda_0_chol), dim = c(irhor, length(lambda_0_chol), length(lambda_0_chol)))

  irhor <- dim(lambda_0[[1]])[1]
  #dim(lambda_0_median)
  band_68 <- solution$bandwith_68
  band_90 <- solution$bandwith_90
  
  n <- dim(lambda_0)[2]  # number of variables
  irhor <- dim(lambda_0)[1]
  
  # Default names if none are supplied
  if (is.null(variable_names)) {
    variable_names <- paste0("Var ", 1:n)
  }
  
  plot_irf <- function(i=1) {
    #trick I just put 0.5 twice
    #main_IV <- lambda_0[, i, "lower", lambda_name]
    main_IV <- lambda_0[, i, index]
    # main_chol <- lambda_0_chol[,i,index]
    # #Normalize IRF
    # main_chol <- as.numeric(main_chol/lambda_0_chol[1,index,index])
 
    #dim(lambda_0_median)
    time_horizon <- 1:irhor
    
    lower_68 <- band_68[, i, "lower", lambda_name]
    upper_68 <- band_68[, i, "upper", lambda_name]
    lower_90 <- band_90[, i, "lower", lambda_name]
    upper_90 <- band_90[, i, "upper", lambda_name]
    
    ggplot() +
      geom_ribbon(aes(x = time_horizon, ymin = lower_90, ymax = upper_90), fill = "blue", alpha = 0.4) +
      geom_ribbon(aes(x = time_horizon, ymin = lower_68, ymax = upper_68), fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.6) +
      #geom_line(aes(x = time_horizon, y = main_chol), color = "darkblue", linetype = 'dashed') +
      geom_line(aes(x = time_horizon, y = main_IV), color = "darkblue", linetype = "solid") +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = 'red') +
      labs(
        title = TeX(variable_names[i]),
        x = "Time",
        y = "Unit Points"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  }
  
  # Generate plots
  plots_list <- lapply(1:n, plot_irf)
  grid_plots <- do.call("grid.arrange", c(plots_list, nrow = 2))
  
  legend_plot <- plot_grid(grid_plots, custom_legend , ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 0.1))

  # Title and final composition
  title <- ggdraw() + draw_label(TeX(shock_label), fontface = 'bold', x = 0.5, hjust = 0.5)
  final_plot <- plot_grid(title, legend_plot, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.1, 1))
  
  return(final_plot)
}

```


```{r}
#solution <-gen_benchmark

plot_irf_from_gen_benchmark_1var <- function(solution,  #irf_cholesky,
                                        variable_names = NULL, shock="price" ) {
  if (shock == "price"){
   shock_label = "Transmission of supply shocks"
  }else if (shock == "gen"){
    shock_label = "Transmission of demand shocks"
  }else{
    return("Invalid shock type. Please use 'price' or 'quantity'.")
  }
  index <- grep(shock, solution$headers_var)
  lambda_name <- sprintf("lambda_0%d", index)
  
  lambda_0 <- solution$lambda_0
  irhor <- dim(lambda_0[[1]])[1]
  #lambda_0 <- solution$median_50
  #lambda_0_chol <-irf_cholesky$irf
  # lambda_0_chol <- irf_cholesky
  # 
  # lambda_0_chol <- array(unlist(lambda_0_chol), dim = c(irhor, length(lambda_0_chol), length(lambda_0_chol)))

  #dim(lambda_0_median)
  band_68 <- solution$bandwith_68
  band_90 <- solution$bandwith_90
  
  n <- dim(lambda_0)[2]  # number of variables
  irhor <- dim(lambda_0)[1]
  
  # Default names if none are supplied
  if (is.null(variable_names)) {
    variable_names <- paste0("Var ", 1:n)
  }
  
  plot_irf <- function(i=1) {
    #trick I just put 0.5 twice
    #main_IV <- lambda_0[, i, "lower"]
    main_IV <- lambda_0[1:20, i, index]
    # main_chol <- lambda_0_chol[,i,index]
    # #Normalize IRF
    # main_chol <- as.numeric(main_chol/lambda_0_chol[1,index,index])
    # 
    #dim(lambda_0_median)
    time_horizon <- 1:irhor
    
    lower_68 <- band_68[, i, "lower"]
    upper_68 <- band_68[, i, "upper"]
    lower_90 <- band_90[, i, "lower"]
    upper_90 <- band_90[, i, "upper"]
    
    ggplot() +
      geom_ribbon(aes(x = time_horizon, ymin = lower_90[1:20], ymax = upper_90[1:20]), fill = "blue", alpha = 0.4) +
      geom_ribbon(aes(x = time_horizon, ymin = lower_68[1:20], ymax = upper_68[1:20]), fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.6) +
      #geom_line(aes(x = time_horizon, y = main_chol), color = "darkblue", linetype = 'dashed') +
      geom_line(aes(x = time_horizon, y = main_IV), color = "darkblue", linetype = "solid") +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = 'red') +
      labs(
        title = TeX(variable_names[i]),
        x = "Time",
        y = "Unit Points"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  }
  
  # Generate plots
  plots_list <- lapply(1:n, plot_irf)
  grid_plots <- do.call("grid.arrange", c(plots_list, nrow = 2))
  
  legend_plot <- plot_grid(grid_plots, custom_legend , ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 0.1))

  # Title and final composition
  #title <- ggdraw() + draw_label(TeX(shock_label), fontface = 'bold', x = 0.5, hjust = 0.5)
  #final_plot <- plot_grid(title, legend_plot, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.1, 1))
  
  return(legend_plot )
}

```
